ops.title: Concurrent-session stale-base snapshots can silently wipe sibling commits' files in shared jj working copies (cc-skills fleet repos); verify releases via the GitHub tree API and diff full stats, never path-scoped
ops.body:
During the 2026-07-17 gd-build rollout, a concurrent session's jj snapshot in cc-skills (stale working-copy base) deleted `tools/gd-build` and `plugin/guides/yml/*` from the commit tree while committing its own unrelated re-render work on top — then pushed. A path-scoped verification diff (`git diff A B -- <the files I cared about>`) hid the wholesale deletion; the push "succeeded" and looked released while GitHub main lacked the entire payload.

**Why:** shared jj working copies between live sessions snapshot whatever the *other* session's base says the tree is — sibling work committed in between reads as deletions. `jj log` showing your commits as ancestors does NOT mean their content survived into the descendant tree.

**How to apply:** after pushing anything that must be consumable from a remote (packs, git+ URL installs), verify the remote tree directly: `gh api "repos/<o>/<r>/contents/<path>?ref=main"`. When checking whether concurrent work clobbered yours, diff the FULL `--stat` between your last-good commit and current main — never scope the diff to the files you expect. Related: [[cc-family-v8-release-mechanics]] (quiescence polls, tight windows, path-scoped commits).
